summary: The Illinois Department of Transportation concurred and noted that during preparation of the Final Statement, the Board of Education District No. 170 reviewed the Roosevelt School property status, and BOR was subsequently asked to opine that the school no longer constituted a Section 4(f) involvement; BOR's November 7, 1974 letter directed that the Park District for Chicago Heights Director was the proper person to make that determination.

B. Public Hearing Comments
A public hearing for the proposed Lincoln Highway (U.S. Route 30) improvement was held on Tuesday, June 20th 1972 at 10:00 o'clock A.M. in the O.W. Huth Upper Grade Center in Matteson, Illinois.
A summary and disposition of the public hearing testimony and petitions or questions received subsequent to the public hearing relative to the proposed improvement immediately follows on page IX- 8 through IX-13.

PUBLIC HEARING
Selection of the Preferred Alternative
Alternative B was laid out in an attempt to minimize the disruption to existing land use by shifting the centerline for the improvement away from the built-up side of the existing roadway in those areas where one side of the right-of-way was open and undeveloped.

During the course of the study, however, subdivisions were created and development took place that mitigated the opportunities sought by this alignment.
Alternative A was designed to place the proposed new centerline generally along the existing centerline, and therefore necessitates comparable takings along both sides of the existing roadway. These required takings, however, are approximately one-half as wide as those that would be needed under the concept of Line B. Alternative A, therefore diminishes the width of takings to a point which permits, in most cases, the existing development along the roadway to continue in use.
As the study progressed, Alternative B was dropped on the basis that it was no longer a practical alternative due to the land development that had occurred along the route. Line A was the only one presented at the public hearing.
Summary of Public Hearing Testimony
The public response to the proposed construction as exhibited at the Public Hearing was favorable. There was concern expressed by several individuals over the ultimate screening of the highway's residential areas, the need for signalization at several of the intersections, and the location of access points to and from the highway. Also, inquiries were made regarding the installation of street lights and the construction of a bike path on the highway right-of-way concurrently with

the highway project. Other questions pertaining to geometrics and right-of-way requirements were made, these being of an individual interest, rather than of a general nature. These questions were raised both verbally at the public hearing and by letter prior to and following the hearing. A copy of the transcript of the hearing included in the appendix. Sepice of all correspondence, both reportation are also included in the appendix.
Following is a summary of the more pertinent points raised at he hearing and the answers given by the Department.
1. A question was raised concerning the possibility of including a bike path with the proposed construction. The Department's response to this was that there was no right-of-way available that would not be used by the highway construction, and that a bike path could not legally be incorporated with the construction unless there is one in existence at the present time.
Questions were raised concerning the design of the roadway drainage system for the new highway. These questions were answered where possible. However, it was pointed out that the drainage design was a part of a later phase of the development of the project and therefore specific detailed features are unknown at this time. It was also stated that the present drainage outfall pattern will be maintained and would be in accordance with the statutes of the State of Illinois.
3. Several individuals and representatives of local municipalities raised questions regarding the destruction of existing screening along Lincoln Highway in the vicinity of Park Forest and along Olympian Way. They

were told that all existing plantings which provide screening will be salvaged where possible. Where this is not practical, substitute planting will be provided.
4. A number of questions were raised regarding access to and from the highway with particular attention given to the new Lincoln Mall, the Korvette plaza, and several other small business enterprises. In all cases, adequate access can be developed and still maintain the degree of safety necessary for a highway of this type. Regarding the installation of traffic signals at access points to major shopping facilities, the Department requested that applications be made to the proper authorities and if the established warrants are met, signals could be installed.
5. Questions were raised concerning the channelization and signalization of intersections with Lincoln Highway at Main, Evergreen, Indiana, and Chestnut Streets. The reply to these inquiries was that all would be channelized and signalization provided where established warrants are met.
6. One resident questioned the need for shifting the centerline of the highway in the vicinity of his home, thereby requiring additional right-of-way to be taken from him resulting in the loss of his shrubbery and trees. He was told that the shift in alignment was necessary to avoid a cemetery on the opposite side of the highway and that he would be compensated for his actual property losses plus all consequential damages that could be justified. It was suggested that with the compensatory adjustment that he would receive, a screening such as a fence could be constructed.

7. A question was raised regarding street lighting and the party was informed that the present policy of the Illinois Department of Transportation requires the local municipality to pay for this installation. It can be made a part of the overall contract for the new highway, providing the municipality is willing to underwrite these costs and that sufficient time is allowed to develop the lighting plans.
8. Several residents raised questions as to why mountable or non-mountable median curbs were specified for various areas. They were told that the major concern was for safety to the motorist and that median types had been specified with this purpose in mind.
9. One representative of a local municipality stated that they were in no position to participate in the cost of utility adjustments made necessary by the construction of the new highway. He was told that he should make this known in writing to the Department of Transportation requesting that the state pay for these adjustments and that this request would then be honored.
10. A representative of the police department stated the need for immediate repairs to the existing pavement and the need for additional traffic control devices. He was told that this was a matter of budgeting maintenance funds and that everything possible would be done to keep the present facility operating efficiently.
11. One resident questioned the need to widen the roadway at all. Traffic projection figures were given as justification for the proposed roadway widths.
12. A question was raised regarding the scheduling of condemnation proceedings for right-of-way. It was stated that the Department

was flexible on this matter since construction was still approximately two years away and that consideration would be given to any reasonable request.
As indicated in the above summary and in the attached transcript and correspondences all legitimate objections have been reviewed and satisfactory agreements reached for each area of concern.

CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS
After consideration of all aspects of the proposed construction as contained in this report including public responses made known at the public hearing, it is concluded that the interests of the public can best be served by reconstructing the existing facility. The present roadway is inadequate, both geometrically and structurally, to meet the demands imposed by traffic and, based on traffic projections, will be totally inadequate in the future.
The design for reconstructing the highway as presented at the public hearing was developed based on sound engineering judgment and meets all the requirements of federal, state and local agencies. All legitimate and reasonable objections raised at the public hearing to the proposed design have been answered and satisfac ory agreements reached.
Based on the foregoing it is recommended that the design as presented at the public hearing be adopted and that the existing roadway and appurtenances be reconstructed in accordance therewith.

a.) Section 4(f) Comments
From the information presented, we agree thet there is no feasible and prudent alternative to the proposed project. The compensation for the right-of-way taken from the yard and playground of the Roosevelt school should be sufficient to provide total payment to the City of Chicago Heights for the portion of Sunnyside Avenue that will be closed to provide replacement land. We would also recommend that the replacement of trees and shrubs and the implementation of other landscaping measures discussed in the Section 4(f) submission be included in the contract plans rather than being included in the right-of-way settlement, if this is agreeable with School District No. 170. If these recommendations and the proposals outlined in the draft Section 4(f) submission are carried out, than we believe that this compensation and replacement will adequately offset the loss of playground.
a.) It has been mutually agreed that the School District be compensated for the replacement of trees and shrubs rather than being included in the contract plans. If landscaping were included in the contract, the property would be affected by requiring a temporary easement to enter onto the property to do the contract items.

During the preparation of the Final Statement a review of the status of the Roosevelt School property involvement was conducted by the Board of Education, District No. 170 (See page G-7). Based upon this determination the U.S. Department of Interior - Bureau of Outdoor Recreation was requested to give opinion that the use of the Roosevelt School no longer constituted a Section 4(f) involvement. In a letter dated November 7, 1974, the United States Department of the Interior stated that the proper person to make a determination of recreation significance would be the Directr of the Park District for Chicago Heights. (See page G-5 and Chapter III, page III-7 for the present status)
